handoff.desc: Once plaintext is delivered, credential leaves the system. We stop monitoring and cannot return the plaintext again.
handoff.title: Handoff

into-bus.desc: Bus manages the credential. Members share it. We keep monitoring liveness.
into-bus.title: Into bus

push-pool.desc: Dual-write into your configured pool. Our copy stays for monitoring.
push-pool.title: Push to my pool

alert.body: The credential is not deleted until confirm. Step 2 is retryable within TTL. After confirm the plaintext is gone.
alert.title: Credential stays until step 3

handoff.code:
# 1. Init → get token
POST /api/me/handoff
{ "credential_ids": ["01H8..."] }

# 2. Use token to fetch plaintext (retryable within TTL)
GET /api/me/handoff/<token>

# 3. Confirm receipt → we then delete
POST /api/me/handoff/<token>/confirm
handoff.sub: Guards against "we deleted the credential but you never received the plaintext"
handoff.title: Handoff is three-phase

alert.part-4: parameter errors — retry will not help

matrix.footnote-1: **session** = browser login only · **API key** = X-API-Key or Authorization: Bearer · most endpoints accept both
matrix.footnote-2: Endpoints with ✓ in **idempotency** require a 32-hex `X-Idempotency-Key` header · replays return byte-identical responses
matrix.footnote-3: Endpoints with ✓ in **paged** return `{ items, total, page, page_size, pages }` · support `?page=&page_size=` (max 500)
matrix.footnote-4: Endpoints with ✓ in **one-shot** return a sensitive field that is only visible in this one response (API key plaintext, webhook secret, handoff plaintext key). Once closed you cannot get it again.
matrix.hero-sub: One row per endpoint. ✓ = required / has it · — = not required / not applicable.

bus.alert: Pulling 1 costs more per credential than a batch. Amounts in the response are final — record them as-is. Channel fees do not apply to pulls, only to top-ups.
bus.response-code:
// Response
{
  "pull_round_id": "01H8...",
  "vendor_id": "<vendor_id>",
  "purchased": 5,
  "credential_ids": ["01H8a", "..."],
  "unit_price": 21000000,        // microunit · final unit price (all line items rolled in)
  "service_fee": 5000000,        // microunit · service fee line, shown separately
  "total_debit": 105000000,      // = unit_price × purchased
  "balance_remaining": 895000000
}
bus.title: Pull for a bus

solo.code:
curl -X POST https://<base-url>/api/me/pull \
  -H "X-API-Key: usr-<your key>" \
  -H "X-Idempotency-Key: $(openssl rand -hex 16)" \
  -d '{"count": 2, "zone": "us"}'
solo.sub-suffix: · credentials go into pull-records for you to assign
solo.title: Solo pull (no bus)

alert.body-2: · cannot change your password or create a new API key — that would let a leaked key lock you out

alert.body: The plaintext key appears only once in the create response. After close it cannot be recovered. Revoke via DELETE — the ledger row is kept (revoked=true) and still appears in the list.
alert.title: One-shot plaintext · soft delete

api-keys.code:
# Create (session only · an API key cannot create a new key)
POST /api/me/api-keys
{ "name": "my-bot" }

# List (API keys can also list · revoked entries included)
GET /api/me/api-keys

# Revoke (soft delete · row kept for audit)
DELETE /api/me/api-keys/<id>
api-keys.title: API key management

error.label: Errors
error.value-suffix: , not by message (message wording will change)

idempotency.code:
KEY=$(openssl rand -hex 16)

curl -X POST https://<base-url>/api/me/buses/<bus_id>/pull \
  -H "X-API-Key: usr-<your key>" \
  -H "X-Idempotency-Key: $KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"count": 3}'

# Network dropped? Replay the same $KEY — no double charge
idempotency.note: Idempotency window is 30 days. After that, the same key is a new request.
idempotency.sub: Same key replayed → byte-identical response · no double side effects
idempotency.title: Using the idempotency key
